grammar.usage:
English: The Present Perfect Tense is formed with 'has/have + past participle'. It connects past actions to the present. In this sentence, 'has been' shows that bungee jumping started being popular in the past (since the 1990s) and continues to be popular now.
中文: 现在完成时由“has/have + 过去分词”构成。它将过去的动作与现在联系起来。在这个句子中，“has been”表示蹦极从过去（自20世纪90年代起）开始流行，并且一直持续到现在。
notes:
English: A common trap is confusing it with the Simple Past. Look for time phrases like 'since', 'for', 'already', 'yet', 'just', 'recently'. 'Since' is followed by a point in time (e.g., 1990s), 'for' is followed by a period (e.g., 10 years).
中文: 一个常见的陷阱是将其与一般过去时混淆。寻找时间短语，如“since”、“for”、“already”、“yet”、“just”、“recently”。“Since”后面跟一个时间点（例如，1990s），“for”后面跟一个时间段（例如，10 years）。

examples.cn: 我已经完成了我的作业。

grammar.title: Passive Voice (Simple Past) / 被动语态（一般过去时）
grammar.titleEn: Passive Voice (Simple Past) / 被动语态（一般过去时）
grammar.usage:
English: The Passive Voice is formed with 'be + past participle'. It emphasizes the action or the receiver of the action rather than the doer. Here, 'was introduced' is the Simple Past Passive. The focus is on 'it' (bungee jumping) and the action of being introduced. The doer (who introduced it) is not mentioned because it's not important.
中文: 被动语态由“be动词 + 过去分词”构成。它强调动作或动作的承受者，而不是执行者。这里，“was introduced”是一般过去时的被动语态。重点是“it”（蹦极）和被引入这个动作。执行者（谁引入了它）没有被提及，因为它不重要。
notes:
English: Remember the structure: be (am/is/are/was/were) + past participle (V-ed/irregular form). A common trap is forgetting to change the 'be' verb according to the tense and subject. Also, the 'by' phrase (to show the doer) is often omitted when the doer is unknown or unimportant.
中文: 记住结构：be动词(am/is/are/was/were) + 过去分词(V-ed/不规则形式)。一个常见的陷阱是忘记根据时态和主语改变be动词。另外，当执行者未知或不重要时，表示执行者的“by”短语经常被省略。

grammar.titleEn: Adverbial Clause of Time (as soon as, the minute) / 时间状语从句（as soon as, the minute）
grammar.usage:
English: 'As soon as' and 'the minute (that)' are conjunctions used to introduce Adverbial Clauses of Time. They mean 'immediately after' or 'at the exact moment when'. The clause they introduce shows the time when the action in the main clause happens. The verb tense in the main clause and the time clause should be logically consistent (often present tense in the time clause for future meaning, or matching past tenses).
中文: 'As soon as'和'the minute (that)'是引导时间状语从句的连词。意思是“……就……”或“在……的那一刻”。它们引导的从句表示主句动作发生的时间。主句和时间从句中的动词时态应该在逻辑上保持一致（时间从句常用现在时表示将来意义，或使用匹配的过去时态）。
notes:
English: Pay attention to tense agreement. For general truths or habitual actions (like in this text), we can use 'would' in the main clause with present tense in the time clause. For future events, use present simple in the time clause and future tense in the main clause (e.g., I will call you as soon as I arrive). Don't use future tense in the 'as soon as' clause.
中文: 注意时态一致。对于普遍真理或习惯性动作（如本文中），我们可以在主句中使用'would'，在时间从句中使用现在时。对于将来事件，在时间从句中使用一般现在时，在主句中使用将来时（例如，我一到就给你打电话）。不要在'as soon as'从句中使用将来时。

grammar.title: Attributive Clause (which) / 定语从句（which）
grammar.usage:
English: An Attributive Clause (or Relative Clause) gives more information about a noun. It usually begins with a relative pronoun like 'which', 'that', 'who', etc. Here, 'which is named after...' is a non-restrictive clause giving extra information about 'wingsuit flying'. It is separated by a comma. 'Which' refers to the thing mentioned before ('wingsuit flying').
中文: 定语从句（或关系从句）提供关于一个名词的更多信息。它通常以关系代词开头，如'which'、'that'、'who'等。这里，“which is named after...”是一个非限制性从句，提供关于“wingsuit flying”的额外信息。它用逗号隔开。“Which”指代前面提到的事物（“wingsuit flying”）。
notes:
English: Key points: 1) Use 'which' for things, 'who' for people. 2) Non-restrictive clauses (with commas) add extra, non-essential info. Restrictive clauses (no commas) give essential info to identify the noun. 3) The relative pronoun should be the subject or object in its own clause. Here, 'which' is the subject of 'is named'.
中文: 关键点：1) 用'which'指物，'who'指人。2) 非限制性从句（有逗号）添加额外的、非必要的信息。限制性从句（无逗号）提供识别名词的必要信息。3) 关系代词在其自己的从句中应充当主语或宾语。这里，“which”是“is named”的主语。

grammar.titleEn: Comparative Form (more + adjective) / 比较级（more + 形容词）
grammar.usage:
English: The Comparative Form is used to compare two things. For most adjectives with two or more syllables (like 'dangerous'), we add 'more' before the adjective, followed by 'than'. The structure is: more + adjective + than. It shows that one thing has a higher degree of the quality than the other.
中文: 比较级用于比较两个事物。对于大多数两个或更多音节的形容词（如“dangerous”），我们在形容词前加“more”，后面跟“than”。结构是：more + 形容词 + than。它表示一件事物比另一件事物具有更高程度的某种品质。
notes:
English: Remember the rules: 1) For one-syllable adjectives, add -er (e.g., fast -> faster). 2) For two-syllable adjectives ending in -y, change -y to -i and add -er (e.g., happy -> happier). 3) For most other adjectives with two or more syllables, use 'more' (e.g., beautiful -> more beautiful). Irregular forms must be memorized (good -> better, bad -> worse).

grammar.title: Although / 虽然 (让步状语从句)
grammar.titleEn: Although / 虽然 (让步状语从句)
grammar.usage:
English: 'Although' is a subordinating conjunction used to introduce a concession or contrast. It means 'in spite of the fact that'. The clause it introduces (the 'although' clause) presents a fact that might make the main clause seem surprising. The main clause often contains 'but' in meaning, but we do NOT use 'but' after a comma when 'although' starts the sentence.
中文: 'Although' 是一个从属连词，用于引导让步或对比。意思是'尽管...'。它引导的从句（'although'从句）陈述一个事实，这个事实可能让主句的内容显得出乎意料。主句在含义上常有'但是'，但当'although'开头时，逗号后我们不能再用'but'。
notes:
English: A common trap is using 'but' after an 'although' clause (e.g., 'Although it was raining, but we went out.' is WRONG). Remember: 'Although/Though' and 'but' cannot be used together in one sentence. Choose one.
中文: 常见陷阱是在'although'从句后使用'but'（例如：'Although it was raining, but we went out.' 是错误的）。记住：'Although/Though' 和 'but' 不能在同一句话中同时使用。二选一。

grammar.titleEn: It is... that... (Emphatic Structure) / 强调句型
grammar.usage:
English: This is the 'It is/was + emphasized part + that/who + rest of the sentence' structure. It is used to give special importance to one part of a sentence (the subject, object, or adverbial). The sentence works normally if you remove 'it is' and 'that'. The word 'that' is usually used, but 'who' can be used for people.
中文: 这是'It is/was + 被强调部分 + that/who + 句子其余部分'的强调句型。用于特别强调句子的某一部分（主语、宾语或状语）。如果去掉'it is'和'that'，句子仍然成立。通常用'that'，但强调人时可用'who'。
notes:
English: Key point: The emphasized part is NOT the subject of the verb after 'that'. The verb form agrees with the original subject. Trap: Confusing it with the 'It is + adjective + to do' structure or a subject clause starting with 'That'.
中文: 关键点：被强调的部分不是'that'后面动词的主语。动词形式与原主语一致。陷阱：与'It is + 形容词 + to do'结构或由'That'开头的主语从句混淆。

grammar.title: No matter how + adjective/adverb / 无论多么...（引导让步状语从句）
grammar.titleEn: No matter how + adjective/adverb / 无论多么...（引导让步状语从句）
grammar.usage:
English: 'No matter how' is used to introduce a clause of concession, meaning 'it does not matter how...'. It emphasizes that the action in the main clause will happen or is true in all situations, regardless of the degree or extent described by the adjective or adverb following 'how'. It is similar to 'However difficult it is,...'.
中文: 'No matter how' 用于引导让步状语从句，意思是'无论多么...'。它强调主句中的动作会在所有情况下发生或是真实的，不管'how'后面的形容词或副词描述的程度如何。它类似于'However difficult it is,...'。
notes:
English: Remember the structure: 'No matter how + adjective/adverb + subject + verb'. The clause can come at the beginning or end of the sentence. Do not confuse 'no matter how' with 'how' in questions. Also, note the use of 'would be' indicates a hypothetical future difficulty.
中文: 记住结构：'No matter how + 形容词/副词 + 主语 + 动词'。从句可以放在句首或句尾。不要将'no matter how'与疑问句中的'how'混淆。另外，注意'would be'的使用表示一种假设的未来困难。

grammar.title: Present Perfect Tense (has/have + past participle) / 现在完成时
grammar.titleEn: Present Perfect Tense (has/have + past participle) / 现在完成时
grammar.usage:
English: The Present Perfect Tense is formed with 'has/have + the past participle' of the main verb. It connects the past and the present. It is often used for: 1) actions that happened at an unspecified time in the past, 2) actions that started in the past and continue to the present, and 3) experiences in one's life up to now. In this sentence, it shows a past action ('attracted attention') with a present result or relevance (the attention is ongoing or affects the present).
中文: 现在完成时由'has/have + 动词的过去分词'构成。它连接过去和现在。常用于：1) 发生在过去不确定时间的动作，2) 从过去开始持续到现在的动作，以及 3) 到目前为止的人生经历。在这个句子中，它表示一个过去动作（'引起了注意'）对现在有结果或影响（这种注意是持续的或影响现在）。
notes:
English: Common traps: 1) Using Present Perfect with specific past time expressions (e.g., 'yesterday', 'last year'). Use Simple Past instead. 2) Forgetting the past participle form of irregular verbs. 3) Confusing it with Simple Past. Remember: Present Perfect focuses on the present result/experience; Simple Past focuses on the finished past action itself.
中文: 常见陷阱：1) 将现在完成时与具体的过去时间状语连用（如'yesterday', 'last year'）。应改用一般过去时。2) 忘记不规则动词的过去分词形式。3) 与一般过去时混淆。记住：现在完成时侧重于现在的结果/经历；一般过去时侧重于已完成的过去动作本身。

grammar.title: Modal Verb 'can' (Ability) / 情态动词'can'（表示能力）
grammar.titleEn: Modal Verb 'can' (Ability) / 情态动词'can'（表示能力）
grammar.usage:
English: The modal verb 'can' is used here to express physical or learned ability in the present. It shows what someone is capable of doing. The structure is 'subject + can + base form of the verb'. It is invariable (no 's' for third person singular). It is followed directly by the main verb without 'to'.
中文: 情态动词'can'在这里用于表达现在身体上或学到的能力。它显示某人能够做什么。结构是'主语 + can + 动词原形'。它是不变的（第三人称单数不加's'）。它后面直接跟主要动词，不加'to'。
notes:
English: Common errors: 1) Adding 'to' after 'can' (e.g., 'can to play' is WRONG). 2) Adding 's' to 'can' for he/she/it (e.g., 'He cans play' is WRONG). 3) Confusing 'can' (ability) with 'could' (past ability or polite request) or 'may' (permission). For future ability, we often use 'will be able to'.
中文: 常见错误：1) 在'can'后加'to'（例如：'can to play'是错误的）。2) 为he/she/it在'can'后加's'（例如：'He cans play'是错误的）。3) 将'can'（能力）与'could'（过去能力或礼貌请求）或'may'（许可）混淆。表示将来能力，我们常用'will be able to'。
